next_steps: Jamie Chen - share Redwood marketplace listing checklist and sample manifest by 2026-03-10
Priya Patel - draft reference architecture doc and upload to shared drive by 2026-03-12
CapstoneCloud (Liam) - provide sample AMI/container image details and billing expectations by 2026-03-11
Schedule joint legal touchpoint (MSA/rev share) - target week of 2026-03-15
action_items: Jamie Chen: send listing checklist, contact for marketplace shepherd (due 2026-03-10)
Priya Patel: create initial reference architecture diagram (due 2026-03-12)
Liam O'Connor: share network/VPC requirements and sample HA setup (due 2026-03-11)

summary: Short sync between Redwood AE/SE and CapstoneCloud to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for private/dedicated customers, and next steps for a joint solution/Go-To-Market. Key asks: listing manifest, billing/metering integration, security docs (SOC2/ISO), and a reference architecture covering Redwood Private and Dedicated options. Agreed next steps and owners for checklist, architecture draft, and legal alignment.
topics: Reference architecture for marketplace customers (VPC, Private, Dedicated)
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 minutes, is that still good for folks?
[00:05] Evan Morales: yeah that's perfect, thanks jamie, appreciate it.
[00:10] Priya Patel: hi, priya here, i'm the se on the account, i'll run through the tech bits and the reference arch.
[00:18] Sofia Nguyen: hey team, sofia, i'll be owning the partnership side and co-marketing.
[00:22] Liam O'Connor: liam from solutions, i'll handle the integration details on our side.
[00:28] Jamie Chen: great, quick agenda: marketplace listing checklist, reference architecture options (public listing vs private/VPC & dedicated), billing/metering, security and legal, then next steps. sound good?
[00:35] Evan: yep.
[00:38] Priya: ok i'm gonna share my screen, uh — if you can't see say so, the doc is in the shared folder (link: https://redwood.app/shared/capstone-marketplace-draft).
[00:46] Liam: can see it.
[00:48] Priya: ok first, listing checklist — typically we need a manifest (container/ami), a short description, pricing model, screenshots, and a support contact. for marketplace specifically there's also a technical verification pass — e.g., quick smoke tests, image signing, and a compatibility matrix.
[01:05] Evan: what's the typical time for approval in your experience?
[01:08] Jamie: usually 2-4 weeks if everything's in order, but with additional legal or security review it can go longer. if we pre-upload the artifacts and the SOC2 docs it speeds up a lot.
[01:17] Sofia: good to know — so we'll prioritize the security pack. do you have a list of exact artifacts?
[01:22] Jamie: yes — checklist i'll share after the call. includes SOC2 report, iso attestation (if available), data flow diagrams, and any KMS/HSM integration notes.
[01:30] Priya: on the technical side, for reference architecture there are a couple patterns we recommend: 1) marketplace listing that deploys to customer VPC (via container/helm/AMI) — typical for Capstone's customers who want private networking; 2) marketplace + Redwood Dedicated behind the scenes where the listing provisions a subscription and we route to dedicated capacity — this is more of a SaaS listed offering with reserved capacity; 3) hybrid where initial deploy is marketplace-managed but critical workloads can be routed to Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC peering.
[01:58] Liam: can you expand on the vpc networking? we run strict egress controls and our customers want private peering.
[02:04] Priya: sure — the VPC option requires a small set of ingress rules for the initial provisioning or you can do an offline install using an airgap bundle. for peering we support VPC peering or private endpoints, and we can surface KMS integrations for customer-managed keys. note: some small level of telemetry/health checks are needed; if customers block that we can provide manual health endpoints.
[02:26] Evan: good. is there any difference for the Dedicated path re: latency/kv cache?
[02:31] Priya: yes, Dedicated gives guaranteed GPU pools and lower latency. we also have tuning knobs for kv cache and batching; for high-throughput inference we push quantized models and larger batch sizes. that will be in the reference arch doc.
[02:45] Jamie: pricing question — marketplace metering vs direct billing — how do you see revenue share?
[02:51] Sofia: our side wants a clear rev share for marketplace sales, and we need the billing reconciliation flow.
[02:56] Jamie: understood. typically marketplaces have a billing abstraction and then pass funds to us, or in some cases you route via capstone's billing. we should loop in legal — but we can agree on a rough split for planning.
[03:08] Liam: technical ask — what does the image look like? do you publish a public container or do we host a private image in our registry?
[03:14] Priya: we can support both. many partners publish a signed image in the marketplace registry. alternatively we can provide a private helm chart or ami bundle that Capstone publishes in the marketplace with instructions for customer registry sync.
[03:26] Evan: ok, for customers who need air-gapped installs what's the process?
[03:30] Priya: we provide an airgap bundle and docs, and the verification tests run locally. there is a bit more manual work but it's supported.
[03:36] Jamie: security/compliance — quick check: you asked for SOC2, sso/saml, RBAC, audit logs?
[03:42] Sofia: yes, SOC2 is priority; also audit logs and SSO (we onboard via SAML).
[03:47] Priya: we have SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO (with IdP metadata), role-based access, and audit log exports. we'll attach redwood security pack. also note we support customer KMS with HSM-backed providers for encryption of keys at rest.
[04:05] Liam: any gotchas on networking for audit log export?
[04:08] Priya: audit logs can be pushed to customer endpoints or pulled via secure APIs. if customers restrict outbound we can use a push into an S3 bucket or a customer log sink. we'll document patterns in the ref arch.
[04:20] Evan: what about performance benchmarks? we have customers who will want 99th percentile latency numbers.
[04:25] Priya: we've got published perf profiles for common open models; for private/dedicated we can run benchmarks on your representative workload. typically we do a joint benchmark run during PoC.
[04:36] Jamie: ok let's talk test plan. proposed: Capstone provides sample workload and image, Redwood runs a smoke test and a perf run in a dedicated environment, and we produce a short report. sound ok?
[04:47] Liam: yes, we'll provide sample queries and expected TTK.
[04:50] Jamie: great. timeline — i'd say checklist by next tuesday, ref arch draft in a week, bench run within two to three weeks after artifacts.
[04:58] Sofia: that aligns with our goal to have a marketplace listing ready in april, so good.
[05:03] Evan: one last item — co-marketing materials and launch plan.
[05:07] Sofia: i'll own that on our side, we'll need logos, a short one-pager and maybe a joint webinar.
[05:13] Jamie: we'll provide a one-pager and a tech blog draft.
[05:17] Priya: quick note - there's sometimes confusion between Redwood "Private" and "Dedicated" naming — i've seen it transcribed as redwood privatey in other notes, just to call out, so in the ref arch we'll label them explicitly (Redwood Private = customer-managed VPC deploy; Redwood Dedicated = reserved GPU pool run by Redwood).
[05:32] Liam: ha yeah we've seen both.
[05:34] Evan: any blockers on the legal/msa side?
[05:36] Jamie: we should loop legal in parallel; i'll introduce our legal contact. marketplaces sometimes require a partner agreement and rev share addendum.
[05:44] Sofia: ok we'll also route to our procurement.
[05:46] Priya: last technical Q — logging and tracing: do you want backtraces or anonymized telemetry?
[05:51] Liam: anonymized telemetry is fine, but customers need access to request-level traces for debugging when they opt in.
[05:57] Priya: ok we'll document opt-in tracing and pseudonymization.
[06:01] Jamie: we're running up on time, quick recap: Jamie to send checklist, Priya to draft reference arch and perf plan, Liam to share images/AMI and network requirements, Sofia to coordinate co-marketing, legal loop for MSA. we'll aim for the timelines we discussed.
[06:18] Evan: thanks all, this was helpful.
[06:21] Jamie: thanks folks, i'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench run and a doc link.
[06:26] Sofia: thanks.
[06:28] Liam: thanks, bye.
[06:30] [call ended]
